narrative: During the 2000s, Black and African women's hairstyles and hair culture continued to thrive, building upon the momentum of the natural hair movement that originated in the 1960s. The afro, a hairstyle created by combing out natural growth or styling with chemical curling products, remained a staple, while cornrows, traditional braids originating from Africa, gained popularity among women seeking protective styles for their Afro-textured hair. Dreadlocks and locs also became increasingly visible, as individuals sought to celebrate their natural textures. Box braids, another protective style, emerged as a popular choice among Black Africans and the African diaspora, offering versatility in styling and ease of maintenance. These hairstyles not only reflected a desire for self-expression but also served as a means of reclaiming and celebrating one's cultural heritage.
